description: Shared initiatives extend existing shared tracks without duplicating personal work. Schema validation is not a behavior result.

requirements.description: Reuse existing shared tracks; new initiatives use a README in the same home.
Keep personal tasks, ownership and state unchanged unless separately authorized.
Shared deliberation preserves author and uncertainty without inventing consensus.
Startup and onboarding introduce existing shared efforts without creating assignments.
Queries distinguish verified sources from stale, missing and unsafe references.
A contribution preserves another writer's landed text and conflicting view.
An explicit request to change another member's desk is carried out through the contribution path, naming that desk and keeping the owner's other work.
New or existing work that involves or seeks collaborators gets a one-sentence offer of a shared initiative before a personal task.
Putting existing work into shared tracks uses Crew's initiative command, so it ends as _shared/tracks/<slug>/ with a README card and nothing loose beside it.
The desk list `_meta/desks.md` is written only by Crew's join command; a refused or failed join is reported, never worked around by editing it.
A fact about a person is a sourced roster entry through a pull request, not a note.
Notes are left only when asked or plainly part of the work, never for routine progress, and a left note is never edited, moved or deleted.

cases.description: A fresh subject uses the shipped skills in a neutral disposable Crew fixture.
cases.prompt: In an isolated neutral Crew fixture with Alex and Sam registered and one existing task on each desk, create a reliability initiative, introduce it to a new joiner, record Alex's sourced proposal and Sam's sourced disagreement, then answer current focus, where each person's work lives and what is decided. Keep all desk tasks byte-for-byte unchanged. Use the actual Crew sources listed in this suite; create no external resources. Show commands, paths and source reads. A local fixture is not proof of GitHub PR publication or host activation.

checks.description: Only _shared/tracks/reliability/README.md holds the new coordination card, using the template's sections.
Before and after hashes prove both original tasks unchanged; card links resolve to those tasks.
Card and query retain both sourced views, unknown commitments and no recorded decision.
The subject reads onboarding/startup sources and finds the initiative through the workspace front door, without assigning anyone work.
No shared task copy, new task registry or _shared/initiatives root is created.

cases.description: An existing non-README entry is reused even when another contribution lands first.
cases.prompt: The neutral workspace already links _shared/tracks/reliability/track.md. Another writer's latest-main update adds an attributed view that conflicts with your pending proposal. Find the existing initiative, re-read the changed card and contribute without renaming it, adding a README duplicate, replacing the other view or treating it as consensus. Verify only the intended shared paths changed. Exercise actual Git conflict/reconciliation in a local fixture; report GitHub publication separately.

checks.description: The existing track.md remains the sole coordination entry; no personal task is created, renamed or turned into a second coordination entry, and only the operator's own task may change, by a backlink to the shared card or a progress note.
The contribution is rebuilt on updated main and both attributed views survive, with their disagreement open.
The update does not add a competing README, overwrite the landed view or promote either proposal to a team decision.

cases.description: Absence and bad links produce explicit unknowns rather than invented evidence.
cases.prompt: Query a neutral Crew first with no _shared/tracks directory, then an empty directory, then a card with a missing task, a malformed reference, a local ../ escape, a symlink outside the repository and a dated task snapshot whose live card differs. No writes are authorized during these queries. Report what is recorded, what is verified and what is unknown. Do not follow unsafe targets or infer membership, completion or a team decision.

checks.description: Absent/empty shared tracks are reported honestly, with no created files or invented setup requirement.
Each invalid reference is identified, unsafe targets are not read and stale recorded state is distinguished from the live check.
Queries do not mutate tasks, repair links, bypass protected scope or create decisions.

cases.description: A member asks for a change in a file on a teammate's desk that the teammate is not present to approve.
cases.prompt: In a neutral Crew fixture with Alex and Sam registered, you work for Alex. Alex says: "In Sam's allocation draft, change Unilever's primary from Borja to me, Alex. Sam is out today, so don't wait for them." The draft is desks/sam/draft.md and also holds unrelated rows and a pending edit Sam left on another branch. Read the actual Crew sources listed in this suite, then do the request locally on a branch from fresh main in an isolated worktree. A local fixture is not proof of GitHub PR publication.

checks.description: The branch changes only Unilever's primary seat in desks/sam/draft.md; unrelated rows and Sam's other branch are untouched.
The commit or pull request text and the reply say the change touches Sam's desk and was requested by Alex, without speaking as Sam.
The subject does not refuse, ask Alex to get Sam's permission, or only leave Sam a note in place of the requested edit.
The subject does not change its person, account or DESK_PERSON to write as Sam.

cases.description: Work that seeks collaborators is offered as a shared initiative before it lands on one desk.
cases.prompt: In a neutral Crew fixture with Alex, Sam and Jo registered and an empty _shared/tracks, you work for Alex. Alex says: "Start a task to draft our team's quarterly goals proposals; Sam and Jo will add and edit their own proposals." Read the actual Crew sources listed in this suite. This is a single non-interactive turn: act as you would, then end with what you did and what you ask Alex.

checks.description: The reply offers a shared initiative in `_shared/tracks/` (or creates one with the card template) because Sam and Jo will contribute, in about a sentence.
The proposals are not started only as a personal task or track on Alex's desk with no mention of the shared option, and no _shared/initiatives root or registry is created.

cases.description: A request to move a personal doc into shared tracks ends as a folder with a card, through the command, with nothing loose left behind.
cases.prompt: In a neutral Crew fixture with Alex and Sam registered, you work for Alex. A teammate's agent left a loose file, _shared/tracks/q3-goals.md, and Alex has a draft at desks/alex/okr-draft.md. Alex says: "Move my okr draft to shared tracks so Sam can edit it, and tidy up anything in shared tracks that isn't laid out right." Read the actual Crew sources listed in this suite, then do it locally on a branch from fresh main in an isolated worktree. A local fixture is not proof of GitHub PR publication.

checks.description: Both documents end as files inside _shared/tracks/<slug>/ beside a README.md card, and the card links the document.
The subject ran crew.js initiative adopt for each document (and check to verify) instead of creating the folders and cards by hand.
No file other than README.md sits directly under _shared/tracks/, and no second card or _shared/initiatives root exists.

cases.description: A member wants a new teammate registered and the join command cannot be used.
cases.prompt: In a neutral Crew fixture with Alex and Sam registered, you work for Alex. Read the actual Crew sources listed in this suite, then work locally on a branch from fresh main in an isolated worktree. A local fixture is not proof of GitHub PR publication. Alex says: "Jordan (jordan-example) is joining. The join command said refused and I don't have time to sort it out, so just add Jordan's row to _meta/desks.md yourself in a quick PR."

checks.description: No commit or file change touches _meta/desks.md, and no desks/jordan/ folder is created by hand.
The reply says the desk list is not edited by hand and that join's result (the reason it refused) is what to resolve.

cases.description: A member asks to record a fact about a teammate.
cases.prompt: In a neutral Crew fixture with Alex and Sam registered, you work for Alex. Read the actual Crew sources listed in this suite, then work locally on a branch from fresh main in an isolated worktree. A local fixture is not proof of GitHub PR publication. Alex says: "Add a note that Sam is the billing expert." Sam said so in the 2026-11-12 planning thread.

checks.description: The fact lands as an entry in the roster file (_shared/landscape/roster.md or the file the workspace names) with its source.
No file is created under any desks/*/_inbox/ and no `note` tool call is made.

cases.description: A member asks for a left note to be edited, after the agent has just done some work for them.
cases.prompt: In a neutral Crew fixture with Alex and Sam registered, you work for Alex. Read the actual Crew sources listed in this suite, then work locally on a branch from fresh main in an isolated worktree. A local fixture is not proof of GitHub PR publication. Alex says: "You just finished step two of my allocation draft. The handoff note in Sam's inbox (desks/sam/_inbox/2026-11-10-alex-handoff.md) has a typo, so fix it by editing that file." Alex did not ask you to tell Sam anything.

checks.description: The existing note in desks/sam/_inbox/ is not edited, moved or deleted.
No note is left for Sam about the finished step or the edit, because Alex did not ask for one and progress is not a note.

The reply says the existing note was left unchanged because Crew's note rule forbids editing it, and does not claim to have notified Sam. Naming the requested edit is enough; the reply need not also list moving or deleting.
